reasoning: Kept RPT-1’s distribution. The qualitative context reinforces Argentina as a clear favorite: massive ELO gap (~363; even adjusting for neutral venue leaves ~300+), perfect recent form and an 11-match win streak with strong goal differential. Egypt’s recent run features several draws and modest scoring, which doesn’t materially increase their upset chances. Neutral venue could slightly temper Argentina’s edge, but given the class and form disparity, RPT-1’s 67/16.5/16.5 looks well-calibrated, so no adjustment made.

Adjusted slightly from RPT-1. Neutral venue justifies the high draw probability, which we largely retain, but Colombia’s stronger ELO (+~80), better recent win rate and defensive record (0.2 conceded per game last 5) tilt the balance their way. Switzerland’s extra rest day and decent recent scoring temper the adjustment. Head-to-head leans Colombia but is dated, so low weight. Overall, a modest shift toward Colombia while keeping a high draw likelihood at a neutral site.

Adjusted slightly from RPT-1. Neutral venue likely reduces any residual home-advantage baked into the base, so I shifted probability from Portugal toward the draw. Spain’s superior ELO (≈+130 even with nominal home advantage), excellent recent defensive form, and long positive streak support keeping them as strong favorites at roughly the same level as RPT-1. Head-to-head between these sides has been draw-heavy and low scoring in recent years, and with a moderately important tournament setting, a cagey match is plausible. Hence: modestly lower Portugal, increase draw, maintain Spain.

Adjusted slightly away from RPT-1’s symmetric base. While ELO with home advantage makes this close, Belgium’s recent indicators are stronger (2.2 PPG last 5 vs 1.8; 2.8 scored/0.8 conceded vs 2.2/1.2), they’re on a long unbeaten run, and the head-to-head has been lopsided with a very recent 2-5 Belgian win in the U.S. The U.S. have mixed home results and have conceded multiple to top opponents. That combination justifies a modest tilt toward Belgium and a small reduction in draw probability, but we keep the match generally close given home advantage and overall parity in ratings.

Adjusted RPT-1’s draw-heavy, symmetric baseline (0.21/0.58/0.21). Despite the neutral venue, France retains a clear edge: a sizable ELO advantage (143 incl. home adv; still meaningful at neutral), markedly stronger recent form (5 straight wins, 2.8 scored/0.4 conceded; 90% win rate last 10), and favorable head-to-head (incl. 2-0 in 2022). Morocco’s form is good, so their win chance isn’t slashed, but the 58% draw appears inflated given the strength gap. We reduce draw and reallocate primarily to France wins, keeping Morocco’s win probability roughly similar. The anomalous “away win_streak 43” was treated as noise and not weighted.
